title: Subordination 4: чтобы vs что
description: что reports a fact and takes an ordinary finite verb (Он сказал, что придёт). чтобы expresses purpose or desire and forces an infinitive or a past-tense verb, never a present or future (Я пришёл, чтобы помочь).
descriptionRussian: что сообщает факт и берёт обычную личную форму глагола (Он сказал, что придёт). чтобы выражает цель или желание и требует инфинитива или прошедшего времени — никогда настоящего или будущего (Я пришёл, чтобы помочь).
intro: Two linking words that look almost identical and do completely different jobs. One reports that something is the case and takes an ordinary verb in any tense. The other expresses a goal or a wish and takes only an infinitive or a past form. The English test is whether 'in order to' or 'so that' would fit. Neither word can be dropped, unlike English 'that'.
rules: что reports a FACT (a statement, knowledge, perception) and takes an ordinary finite verb in any tense: Он сказал, что придёт; Я знаю, что ты был там.
чтобы expresses a GOAL or DESIRE (purpose 'in order to,' or a wish about an action) and takes ONLY an infinitive or a past-tense verb - never a present or future finite verb.
Purpose with чтобы + infinitive when the same person acts: Я пришёл, чтобы помочь (I came in order to help).
Quick test: if English fits 'in order to' or 'so that,' use чтобы; if it just reports that something is the case, use что.
Both clauses are set off by a comma, and neither что nor чтобы can be dropped the way English drops 'that': Он сказал, что придёт (not *Он сказал придёт).
examples: Он сказал, что придёт завтра. (He said that he will come tomorrow.) - fact, что + finite future.
Я думаю, что она права. (I think that she is right.) - fact, что + finite present.
Я пришёл, чтобы помочь. (I came in order to help.) - goal, чтобы + infinitive.
Он работает, чтобы заработать денег. (He works in order to earn money.) - goal, чтобы + infinitive.
Он сказал, что пришёл. (He said that he had come - a fact.) vs Он сказал это, чтобы помочь. (He said it in order to help - a goal.)
Я знаю, что ты был там. (I know that you were there.) - fact, что + finite past.

rows.label: что
cells: Он сказал, что придёт. (He said he would come.)

rows.label: чтобы
cells: Я пришёл, чтобы помочь. (I came to help.)

items.promptEnglish: He said that he would call in the evening.
items.hint: Is this reporting a fact (what he said), or stating a goal? Try 'in order to.'
items.explanation: This reports a FACT - what he said.Что introduces the reported statement, and the verb is an ordinary finite future: позвонит. 'In order to' does not fit ('He said in order to call' makes no sense), so it cannot be чтобы.

items.prompt: Я приехал в Москву, _____ найти работу.
items.promptEnglish: I came to Moscow in order to find a job.
items.hint: What was the PURPOSE of coming to Moscow? 'In order to' fits.
items.explanation: This states the GOAL of coming to Moscow, so чтобы. And чтобы takes the infinitive найти (in order to find), because the same person who came is the one finding work. 'In order to find a job' is the giveaway.

items.promptEnglish: I hope that everything will be fine.
items.hint: надеяться here reports an expectation about a fact. Is there a goal directed at an action?
items.explanation: надеяться, что reports a hoped-for fact, with an ordinary finite verb: будет (will be). This is a statement about how things will be, not a purpose, so что is correct. (After надеяться you would only use чтобы to express a wish aimed at someone's action, which is not the case here.)

items.promptEnglish: She opened the window in order to air out the room.
items.hint: Why did she open the window? The clause states the purpose.
items.explanation: The clause gives the PURPOSE of opening the window, so чтобы + infinitive проветрить. The same person opens and airs out, so the infinitive is correct. 'In order to air out the room' confirms the goal reading.

items.promptEnglish: I see that you are tired.
items.hint: видеть here reports a perceived fact. Is there any goal?
items.explanation: видеть, что reports a perceived FACT - that you are tired. The verb устал is an ordinary finite past form. There is no purpose, so что, not чтобы. Verbs of perception (видеть, слышать, замечать) take что.

items.prompt: Он говорил тихо, _____ не разбудить ребёнка.
items.promptEnglish: He spoke quietly in order not to wake the child.
items.hint: Why did he speak quietly? Negative purpose still uses the same connector.
items.explanation: This is a negative PURPOSE - the goal of speaking quietly was not to wake the child.Чтобы + (не) + infinitive: чтобы не разбудить. Purpose, even negative, takes чтобы plus the infinitive when the subject is the same.

items.promptEnglish: He called in order to warn us.
items.hint: Purpose with the same subject: which connector + form?
items.explanation: Purpose takes чтобы, and with the same subject an infinitive follows: чтобы предупредить. Что reports facts and needs a finite verb; чтобы + past would signal a different subject.

items.promptEnglish: He called and said that he would be late.
items.explanation: A reported fact takes что + a finite verb: сказал, что опоздает. Чтобы would turn it into a goal or demand; the infinitive cannot follow что.

items.promptEnglish: I think that she is right.
items.explanation: Thinking reports a fact: думаю, что она права. Чтобы would demand a wish reading and a past-tense verb; правой is the wrong case for the short predicative.

blanks: Я уверен, _____ он справится с этой задачей. (I am sure that he will manage this task.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: уверен, что reports a fact (a conviction about what will happen), with an ordinary finite verb справится. There is no purpose here, so что, not чтобы. The 'in order to' test fails, confirming что.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I came in order to help you.
errorCorrection.explanation: This states the PURPOSE of coming ('in order to help'), and the goal construction is чтобы plus an infinitive: чтобы помочь.Что reports a fact and takes a finite verb, so it cannot sit in front of the bare infinitive помочь.Как would mean 'how,' and потому что 'because' gives a cause rather than a purpose, neither of which matches the 'in order to' sense the infinitive carries here.
errorCorrection.hint: Does 'in order to' fit? Then it is the goal connector, not the fact connector.

errorCorrection.sentence: Он сказал, чтобы он уже закончил работу.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: He said that he had already finished the work.
errorCorrection.explanation: Here he is REPORTING a fact, that the work is already done, so the connector is что plus a finite verb: что он уже закончил.Чтобы would turn the clause into a goal or a demand ('so that he would finish'), which the past statement does not mean.Как ('how') and будто ('as if') also shift the sense away from a plain report of what was said.
errorCorrection.hint: Is this reporting what happened, or stating a goal? A finished fact takes the fact connector.

errorCorrection.sentence: Она сказала, чтобы она занята сегодня.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: She said that she was busy today.
errorCorrection.explanation: She is reporting a fact about her state, that she is busy, so the connector is что plus a finite clause: что она занята.Чтобы expresses a goal or wish and demands an infinitive or a past-tense verb, so it cannot introduce the plain present-tense statement занята.Как would ask 'how' and если 'if,' neither of which reports the fact that she stated.
errorCorrection.hint: She is stating a fact about herself, not a goal. Which connector reports a fact?

errorCorrection.sentence: Мы встали рано, что успеть на поезд.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: We got up early in order to catch the train.
errorCorrection.explanation: Getting up early is done for a PURPOSE, to catch the train, and purpose is чтобы plus an infinitive: чтобы успеть.Что reports a fact with a finite verb and cannot precede the bare infinitive успеть.Потому что ('because') would give the cause for getting up rather than its goal, and поэтому ('therefore') introduces a result, so neither expresses 'in order to.'
errorCorrection.hint: Why did they get up early? 'In order to' signals the goal connector.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I heard that the concert was cancelled.
errorCorrection.explanation: After слышать ('hear') reporting a piece of news, the connector is что plus a finite verb: что концерт отменили. The clause states a fact that was heard, not a goal, so чтобы is wrong even though отменили looks like a past tense, because here it is the genuine reported past, not the subjunctive чтобы would require.Как ('how') and будто ('as if, supposedly') would colour the report differently and are not the neutral fact connector.
errorCorrection.hint: You heard a fact, not a goal. Which connector introduces reported news?

minimalPairs.context: Он позвонил, _____ предупредить нас. (He called in order to warn us.)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: He called in order to warn us.
minimalPairs.explanation: The clause gives the PURPOSE of calling (in order to warn), so чтобы + infinitive предупредить.Что would report a fact, but here we have a goal with an infinitive. 'In order to warn us' is the test.

minimalPairs.context: Он позвонил и сказал, _____ опоздает. (He called and said that he would be late.)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: He called and said that he would be late.
minimalPairs.explanation: Here he REPORTS a fact - that he will be late - so что + finite verb опоздает. There is no purpose to express; he is simply stating what is the case. Same verb сказать, but this is a fact (что), not a goal (чтобы).

reviewVocab.definition: the conjunction 'that': introduces a reported fact (a statement, knowledge, or perception) and takes an ordinary finite verb in any tense.
reviewVocab.example: Он сказал, что придёт. Я знаю, что это правда.

reviewVocab.definition: 'in order to / so that': introduces a goal or desire and takes ONLY an infinitive (same subject) or a past-tense verb (different subject), never a present or future finite verb.
reviewVocab.example: Я пришёл, чтобы помочь. Он работает, чтобы заработать.

reviewVocab.definition: the quick test: if the English fits 'in order to' or 'so that,' the clause is a goal (чтобы); if it just reports that something is the case, it is a fact (что).
reviewVocab.example: Он сказал это, чтобы помочь (goal) vs Он сказал, что пришёл (fact).
